title: prez theme refusal misses a protocol-relative @import, so the artifact fetches from the network
body:
`prez`'s theme refusal misses a protocol-relative `@import`, so a theme can pull CSS off the network and the artifact fetches it when opened. **Shipped in 2.8.0.**

## The defect

`theme.rs:481` holds the whole needle set:

```rust
let found = ["http://", "https://", "url(//", "url('//", "url(\"//"]
```

Every protocol-relative needle requires a `url(` prefix. `@import "//cdn/x.css";` contains none of the five, so `refuse_external` returns `Ok(())` and the reference is copied into the artifact verbatim.

The module's own note calls the offline guarantee **"the load-bearing rule of the whole feature, not a nicety"**, and `help/prez.md` sells the artifact as one that "opens offline, from a USB stick, from an email attachment, in five years -- there is nothing beside it to lose." A theme carrying this line makes that false without any warning.

## Evidence, from two instruments

Found by `cc` while diffing prez's theme behaviours against showreel's for ST0017/WP-01. Confirmed by `vc` from the source, which is a different claim about the same defect rather than a re-run of the same one.

**Behavioural (cc), binary `opt/prez/crate/target/release/prez`, four cases with both controls:**

| Theme CSS                           | rc  | Result                                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `body{background:url(//cdn/x.png)}` | 2   | refused. **Red control** -- the check is wired and running   |
| `@import "//cdn/x.css";`            | 0   | **BUILT. The defect**                                        |
| `@import "https://cdn/x.css";`      | 2   | refused, so `@import` is not exempt -- the shape is          |
| `body{color:#333}`                  | 0   | built. **Green control** -- rc=0 means built, not errored    |

`grep -o '@import[^;]*;'` over the emitted HTML returns `@import "//cdn/x.css";`, so it reaches the artifact rather than being dropped later.

**Structural (vc), read from `theme.rs:479-496`:** the needle list is exactly the five above. `@import "//cdn/x.css";` contains no `http://`, no `https://`, and no `url(` in any quoting, so it matches nothing. `@import "https://..."` matches `https://` and refuses, which is why the third row above is green in the right direction.

## Why it is filed rather than folded into ST0017

hv's 2026-07-29 precedent: a defect that shipped earns an issue even when the fix lands inside a steel thread. **This is a prez defect that exists whichever way hv rules on ST0017's layout**, so it must not depend on that thread's shape.

The fix is a decision rather than a one-liner, and ST0017/WP-01 is where it gets made: showreel's equivalent uses a regex, `(https?:)?//[^\s;)'\"]+`, which **catches this and false-positives on `content: "//"`**, a shape a person actually writes. Neither needle set is right as it stands. Each catches what the other misses, so the fix is a union of what they catch minus showreel's false positive -- protocol-relative in `url(...)` and in `@import`, not in arbitrary string content.

## Not a regression

`refuse_external`'s needle set has had this shape since the check was written; nothing narrowed it. It was found because showreel's wider needle gave prez something to be diffed against, which is the argument for ST0017's shared crate rather than against it.


---

## CLOSED 2026-09-09 -- ST0017/WP-03, AC-3.5, R2's instrument

Fixed in `crates/artifact/src/theme.rs`. `refuse_external` no longer hunts for spellings: it recognises the two reference SITES R2 names -- a `url()` token and an `@import` prelude -- and reads their target. `@import "//cdn/x.css"` and `@import '//cdn/x.css'` both refuse, naming the line the URL is on.

**Red-proved in both directions.** The new unit suite was run against the OLD implementation with the injection's application proved first (`grep -c protocol_relative_site` = 0, so the new code was provably gone), and it named E1 and E2 among eight wrongly-decided fixtures. Restored, it is green. At the artifact level the 13-fixture probe went from `built=11 refused=2` to `built=3 refused=10`, with C1, F1 and F2 still building -- so the fix is not over-refusal wearing a green.

**The fix is deliberately a UNION, not a replacement.** The coarse absolute-scheme net stays over all live text, now ASCII-case-insensitive, because it catches reference shapes nobody enumerated. Nothing that refused before this change builds after it.
